To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a type I RO based PLL with a SSPD that achieves low jitter and low reference spur performance.

a 0.008 mm2 2. 4GHz type I RO PLL is presented that achieves low jitter thanks a wide bandwidth type I architecture, low reference spurs by using a sub-sampling phase detector and low area by not using an integrating capacitor.
a ring oscillator PLL with sub sampling phase detector has low area and low jitter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a PLL that has low jitter and low power.
the design of a low power low phase noise PLL for a 2.4Ghz WLAN application.
the design, implementation and measurement of a 2.4 GHz type I ring oscillator PLL with a sub sampling phase detection scheme.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a RO based PLL with a type I architecture combined with SSPD is an excellent choice when low area and low jitter is needed.
this work presents a low area, low power, low jitter and low spurs PLL with wide tuning range.
the presented RO based PLL is the best in terms of power consumption, chip area and FoMjitters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a RO based PLL is a good choice for a low power, low noise and low spur PLL.
the presented RO PLL achieves a very high FoMjitter, low area, low power consumption and high phase noise at a low frequency.
the proposed RO based PLL with SSPD has a good balance between area, power, jitter, and reference spurs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sub-sampling can be used in PLLs with type I architectures and that it is possible to achieve very high FoMs in a low power PLL.
sub sampling phase detectors can achieve low reference spurs with low area and low power.
sub sampling PLLs can be used in a type I PLL architecture to achieve low area and low power consumption while maintaining low jitter and low reference spur performance.
